NRL Casualty Ward: Fresh Reynolds injury; Ramien's season over
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.
"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.
"His return-to-play timeline will be determined on a week-by-week basis."
Cronulla Jesse Ramien has also played his final game for the club with the centre undergoing season-ending pectoral surgery on Thursday.
Ramien suffered the injury in the second half of last week's loss to St George Illawarra and will depart the Sharks at the end of the season to join the Cowboys.
"A big blow for the Sharks with Jesse Ramien ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season after undergoing pectoral repair surgery today," the club said in a statement.
"The star centre hurt himself in the second half against the Dragons on Sunday afternoon; he then went for scans on Monday, but after seeing a specialist, it was decided the best course of action was surgery."

The Rooster was named to return after missing last week's win over the Bulldogs but was ruled out of the CommBank Stadium clash on Wednesday night.
The Panthers are missing captain Isaah Yeo due to a pectoral injury suffered in last week's loss to the Warriors.

The second game of NRL action on Friday night will take place in Sydney as the Bulldogs host the Rabbitohs . With both teams flirting with the edge of the Top 8, this game is worth more than just the two competition points as the winner could be set on a path towards the NRL Finals. This ensures that a thrilling contest awaits, and fans will be on the edge of their seats for this match. Before You Bet is here with a detailed look at what is ahead in this contest.

Bulldogs vs Rabbitohs Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
Coming up short
The Bulldogs needed a win last week against the Roosters but failed to demonstrate experience and poise when it mattered most. Trailing 8-2 at HT, they pulled their way back into the match to lead 18-8 with 15 minutes remaining. The fast finish of their opponents meant they were unable to halt their momentum, as a horror completion rate (66%), lack of power (7.8m per carry), and 31 missed tackles hurt their momentum. Despite their poor finish, they can take positives away from the match as their attack continued to improve and pressured the Roosters in areas other teams haven’t been able to achieve.
Scraping home (in style)
Up 28-nil at HT against the Eels, the Rabbitohs were flying and looked every bit a quality team that could cause headaches for other teams inside the Top 8. Unfortunately, their scoring stopped, and they came out a vastly different team in the second half, eventually prevailing 28-24. The win saw them only control 46% possession and complete at 80%, continually making mistakes in the second half to give their opponents key territory. The finish shouldn’t eliminate the positives either. Their 10.1m per carry, 11 line breaks, and just 24 missed tackles are positive points to build upon in coming weeks.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 5 where the Rabbitohs were victorious 32-24. They have a slightly better record at this ground, winning 57% of matches compared to the Bulldogs 54%.
- In the past 5 matches, 4 games have been decided by 8 points or less. The average margin is still high (10.8 points) courtesy of a blowout 32-point win. The average total points in the same games is 46.8 points.
- The Rabbitohs have the superior attacking this season compared to the Bulldogs (19ppg vs 27ppg) but the Bulldogs are stronger defensively (22pg vs 24ppg) by allowing fewer points.
A close call
There is more than just 2 competition points on the line in this game, with a spot in the Finals likely decided upon this result. The Bulldogs have an edge and are listed as favourites. Their resurgence in positive form has many overlooking their shortcomings. While good last week, they gave up a winning chance. If they can produce that same standard here, they are a strong winning hope. The Rabbitohs have numerous flaws but seem to get ‘up’ for bigger matches. Their depth will be further challenged ahead of this match as Ward is replaced by Sullivan at halfback; the return of Graham boosts their edge and their bench, as Gray moves back there.
This game will go down to the wire. The Rabbitohs can bring a defensive pressure when needed and the Bulldogs will relish this challenge. Providing they can eliminate their mistakes, the Rabbitohs are a chance of winning this contest. So too are the Bulldogs but their recent form has reduced the attention on their shortcomings. The odds should have the two teams closer than what they are but rather than chase an upset victory, play it safe and invest on this game to be a thrilling contest that is only decided in the remaining few minutes.

Bulldogs v Rabbitohs: Jones steps up; Sullivan steers ship
The Bulldogs and Rabbitohs renew their fierce rivalry at Accor Stadium, the venue of their 2014 grand final clash and the infamous 2015 Good Friday showdown.
Plenty of water has flowed under the bridge since then but history tells us the Bulldogs have not been back to a grand final since 2014 and the Rabbitohs only once, when they lost to Penrith in 2021.
The Bulldogs were riding high heading into last week's clash with the Roosters and will be left to rue the one that got away after they led 18-8 with 15 minutes to play.
The Rabbitohs raced to a big lead of their own on Saturday night against the Eels (28-0) before falling in a hole and almost allowing the biggest comeback in NRL history to play out.
In the end it took a miraculous 40-20 kick from Cody Walker in the 79th minute to ensure the Bunnies would hold on to seventh spot with four games to play.

A team of two halves

With just 46% possession and a 79% completion rate, they couldn’t turn their 9.6m per carry into more points. Quality and execution to determine the winner

There is no doubt that they will be motivated ahead of this contest but the relentless pressure the Warriors build in their play should expose the lack of maturity the Broncos possess.
